questions.question: An electromagnetic wave is produced by:
Electromagnetic waves need no medium because:
options: The oscillating electric and magnetic fields regenerate each other outward through space
They travel too fast to notice a medium
They are made of tiny particles of air

questions.question: In a vacuum, the speed of a gamma ray compared with a radio wave is:
options: Exactly the same — 3 × 10⁸ m·s⁻¹ for every member of the family

questions.question: The dual nature of electromagnetic radiation means that:
options: It has two frequencies at once
It travels in two directions at once
It can be either transverse or longitudinal
The wave model explains reflection, refraction, diffraction and interference, while the particle (photon) model explains emission, absorption and the ejection of electrons

questions.question: The spectrum from LOWEST to HIGHEST frequency is:
options: Radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma rays
Gamma rays, X-rays, ultraviolet, visible, infrared, microwave, radio
Radio, infrared, microwave, visible, X-rays, ultraviolet, gamma rays
Visible, infrared, ultraviolet, radio, microwave, X-rays, gamma rays

questions.question: Within visible light, the colour with the LONGEST wavelength and LOWEST frequency is:
Moving from radio waves towards gamma rays, wavelength and frequency:
options: Run in opposite directions — the wavelength shortens while the frequency rises, since their product must stay equal to c

questions.question: The IONISING members of the electromagnetic family — those energetic enough to strip electrons off atoms — are:

subtopics.title: The Two Equations — c = fλ and E = hf

questions.question: An FM broadcast at 100 MHz has a wavelength of:
Ultraviolet radiation of wavelength 250 nm must be substituted as:
Ultraviolet of wavelength 2,5 × 10⁻⁷ m has a frequency of:
Using h = 6,63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s, the energy of one photon of frequency 1,2 × 10¹⁵ Hz is:
options: 7,96 × 10⁻¹⁹ J — E = hf, and photon energy is measured in joules

questions.question: Why are X-rays used to image bone while radio waves are not?
options: X-ray photons carry enough energy to penetrate soft tissue and be stopped by bone, while radio photons pass through harmlessly and carry no such information
Radio waves cannot leave the aerial
Bone reflects radio waves too strongly

questions.question: A microwave oven heats food because:
options: The waves burn the outside of the food
Water molecules in the food absorb microwaves strongly and heat up

questions.question: Which statement about ultraviolet radiation is correct?
options: It is harmless because we cannot see it
It travels slower than visible light in a vacuum
It is useful for sterilising and vitamin D production, but causes sunburn, cataracts and skin cancer because it is ionising
It is only produced by hospital equipment

questions.question: The commonest calculation trap in this topic is:
options: Quoting the answer with a unit
Substituting prefixes unconverted — putting 250 into E = hc/λ instead of 2,5 × 10⁻⁷ m

questions.question: The one thing every member of the electromagnetic family shares is:
options: Its speed in empty space — three hundred million metres every second

questions.question: 'Infra-red' and 'ultra-violet' are useful names because they tell you:
options: Where each sits relative to visible light — infrared just below red, ultraviolet just beyond violet

questions.question: If they all move at the same speed, the only real difference between a radio wave and a gamma ray is:
options: How tightly packed they are — long and lazy at one end, short and sharp at the other

questions.question: The 'see-saw' idea says that because the speed is fixed:
options: Shorter waves must arrive more often — wavelength down means frequency up, always
Frequency and wavelength both rise together

questions.question: A microwave oven runs at nearly two and a half billion cycles a second, giving waves about 12 cm long. The door mesh keeps them in because:
options: The metal absorbs all the energy
The holes are far smaller than the waves, so the waves cannot pass through
The waves are slowed by the mesh

questions.question: The 'punch' idea explains that:
options: Shorter, sharper waves carry more energy per packet — one ultraviolet packet carries roughly twelve million times the punch of one radio packet
All packets carry the same energy

questions.question: Sharing three hundred million metres per second among a hundred million radio waves each second gives a wavelength of:
options: 3 m — about the size of a car aerial

subtopics.title: Sunscreen, the Remote and the Lead Apron

questions.question: A TV remote control works using:
You wear a lead apron for a dental X-ray because:
options: X-rays that pass through soft tissue can damage cells on the way, and lead absorbs them
The apron blocks the visible light

questions.question: Gamma rays are deliberately used in hospitals to:
options: Kill cancer cells in radiotherapy and sterilise surgical equipment

questions.question: Sunscreen and a hat matter in South Africa even on a cloudy day because:
options: Ultraviolet still reaches you through cloud, and it is ionising enough to cause sunburn, eye damage and skin cancer
